children.summary: The text discusses U.S. and foreign income before taxes for fiscal years 2023-2025, showing increases in both. U.S. income rose from $52,917 million in 2023 to $62,886 million in 2024 and $69,212 million in 2025; foreign income increased from $36,394 million to $44,901 million and $54,415 million; total income before taxes grew from $89,311 million to $107,787 million and $123,627 million. The effective tax rate decreased from 19.0% in 2023 to 18.2% in 2024 and 17.6% in 2025, with the federal statutory rate at 21.0% each year. Key adjustments include foreign earnings taxed at lower rates (-1.5% in 2025), FDII deduction (-1.0%), state taxes (+1.5%), R&D credit (-1.1%), stock-based compensation benefits (-0.9%), interest (+1.0%), and other items (-1.4%). The decrease is primarily due to earnings taxed at lower rates in foreign jurisdictions, especially through the Ireland regional operations center, which generated 81%, 83%, and 81% of foreign income before tax in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively. Net deferred income tax assets increased from $19,652 million in 2024 to $26,273 million in 2025, with total deferred tax assets of $47,112 million (net of $1,169 million valuation allowance) and deferred tax liabilities of $19,670 million; largest asset components include capitalized R&D ($16,891 million) and leasing liabilities ($12,874 million). As of June 30, 2025, federal, state, and foreign net operating loss carryforwards were $390 million, $836 million, and $2.6 billion, respectively. Federal capital loss carryforwards were $816 million, expiring in fiscal year 2030. Income taxes paid, net of refunds, were $28.7 billion, $23.4 billion, and $23.1 billion in fiscal years 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.

children.summary: The text discusses Microsoft's unrecognized tax benefits, which were $24.7 billion, $22.8 billion, and $17.1 billion as of June 30, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively. If recognized, these would affect effective tax rates by $21.2 billion, $19.6 billion, and $14.4 billion for those years. Accrued interest expense related to uncertain tax positions was $8.2 billion, $6.8 billion, and $5.2 billion for the same periods, with provisions for income taxes including interest expense of $1.3 billion, $1.5 billion, and $918 million. The gross unrecognized tax benefits increased from $17,120 million in 2023 to $22,760 million in 2024, then to $24,729 million in 2025, with current-year increases of $2,066 (2025) and $1,903 (2024), prior-year increases of $468 (2025) and $4,289 (2024), and settlements decreasing by $240 (2025) and $76 (2024). Microsoft is under IRS audit for tax years 2014-2017 and received Notices of Proposed Adjustment for 2004-2013 seeking an additional $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest, which they plan to contest. Unearned revenue by segment increased from $60,184 million in 2024 to $67,265 million in 2025, with Productivity and Business Processes rising from $43,599 million to $50,567 million, Intelligent Cloud from $13,683 million to $14,022 million, and More Personal Computing falling from $2,902 million to $2,676 million. The changes in unearned revenue show a beginning balance of $60,184 million, $186,957 million deferred, $179,876 million recognized, and an ending balance of $67,265 million. Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations was $375 billion as of June 30, 2025, with $368 billion related to commercial revenue, and about 40% expected to be recognized over the next 12 months. The text also mentions lease terms and expenses.

children.summary: The text discusses lease costs, supplemental cash flow and balance sheet information, and future minimum lease payments for operating and finance leases. Operating lease cost increased from $2,875 million in 2023 to $3,555 million in 2024 and $5,524 million in 2025. Total finance lease cost rose from $1,853 million in 2023 to $2,534 million in 2024 and $4,825 million in 2025. Cash paid for operating leases was $4,931M in 2025, $3,550M in 2024, and $2,706M in 2023. Right-of-use assets obtained for operating leases were $7,826M, $6,703M, $3,514M; for finance leases $20,511M, $11,633M, $3,128M. As of June 30, 2025, operating lease right-of-use assets were $24,823 million and total operating lease liabilities $22,861 million; finance lease property and equipment net was $44,015 million with total finance lease liabilities of $46,172 million. Weighted average remaining lease terms are 6 years (operating) and 13 years (finance); discount rates are 3.5% and 4.2%. Future minimum lease payments total $25,481 million for operating leases (imputed interest $2,620 million) and $60,506 million for finance leases (imputed interest $14,334 million). Additional leases not yet commenced total $92.7 billion. The text also covers contingencies: the Irish Data Protection Commission matter involving LinkedIn, and other legal contingencies with accrued liabilities of $541 million and reasonably possible losses up to $600 million beyond recorded amounts.

children.summary: The document reports Microsoft's common stock outstanding for fiscal years 2025, 2024, and 2023, with beginning balances of 7,434, 7,432, and 7,464 million shares, respectively. Issuances were 31, 34, and 37 million, while repurchases were 31, 32, and 69 million, resulting in ending balances of 7,434, 7,434, and 7,432 million shares. It details share repurchase programs: a $60.0 billion program approved on September 14, 2021, completed in April 2025, and another $60.0 billion program approved on September 16, 2024, with $57.3 billion remaining as of June 30, 2025. Quarterly repurchases for fiscal years 2025, 2024, and 2023 totaled 31, 32, and 69 million shares, respectively, with total costs of $13,000 million, $11,960 million, and $18,400 million. The highest quarterly repurchase amount was $4,600 million in 2023. Repurchases were made with cash resources, excluding shares repurchased to settle employee tax withholding of $5.4 billion, $5.3 billion, and $3.8 billion for fiscal years 2025, 2024, and 2023. Dividends declared were $0.83 per share for FY2025 (total $3.32, amount $24,678 million) and $0.75 per share for FY2024 (total $3.00, amount $22,295 million). Accumulated other comprehensive loss components changed: derivatives from $(3) to $(8) in 2025, investments from $(2,625) to $(1,051), translation adjustments from $(2,962) to $(2,288), with total end-of-period losses of $(3,347) in 2025, $(5,590) in 2024, and $(6,343) in 2023. Stock-based compensation expense rose from $9,611 million in 2023 to $10,734 million in 2024 and $11,974 million in 2025; income tax benefits increased from $1,651 million to $1,826 million and $2,027 million over the same periods. Stock awards generally vest over four or five years.

children.summary: The text describes Microsoft's stock-based compensation plans, including the Executive Incentive Plan, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), and savings plans. It details the vesting of RSUs and PSUs, with RSUs vesting over four years and PSUs over three years. The fair value of stock awards was estimated using assumptions: dividends per share ranged from $0.62 to $0.83 quarterly across fiscal years 2023-2025, with 2025 at $0.75–$0.83, 2024 at $0.68–$0.75, and 2023 at $0.62–$0.68. Interest rates ranged from 2.0% to 5.6%, with 2025 at 3.4%–5.5%, 2024 at 3.8%–5.6%, and 2023 at 2.0%–5.4%. In fiscal 2025, nonvested stock awards activity: beginning balance 88 million shares at $292.28 weighted average grant-date fair value, 39 million granted at $413.90, 38 million vested at $293.25, 7 million forfeited at $317.23, ending balance 82 million shares at $347.44. Unrecognized compensation costs were $21.6 billion as of June 30, 2025, expected to be recognized over three years. Weighted average grant-date fair value of awards granted was $413.90, $339.46, and $252.59 for fiscal years 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively. Fair value of vested awards was $16.2 billion, $16.0 billion, and $11.9 billion for the same years. 98 million shares were authorized for future grant. The ESPP allows employees to purchase shares at 90% of fair market value, with purchases limited to 15% of gross compensation. Employees purchased 6 million shares in both fiscal 2025 and 2024, and 7 million in 2023, with average prices of $385.10, $339.46, and $245.59 respectively. 62 million shares were reserved for future issuance through ESPP. Savings plans match employee contributions; employer-funded retirement benefits were $1.8 billion, $1.7 billion, and $1.6 billion in fiscal years 2025, 2024, and 2023. The company's segments are Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing, with operating income as the primary profitability measure.

children.summary: The text is an excerpt from an audit report. The auditor states that they audited the company's internal control over financial reporting as of June 30, 2025, and expressed an unqualified opinion. The basis for opinion explains that the financial statements are management's responsibility and the auditor's responsibility is to express an opinion. The audit was conducted in accordance with PCAOB standards. The report then discusses a critical audit matter regarding revenue recognition, which involves significant judgment in determining distinct performance obligations, pattern of delivery, contract terms, and stand-alone selling prices. The auditor's procedures included evaluating management's judgments.

children.summary: The audit report covers procedures for testing revenue recognition, including identification of performance obligations, timing of revenue recognition, and estimation of variable consideration. It also addresses income taxes, specifically uncertain tax positions related to transfer pricing issues with the IRS for tax years 2004-2013. The company received Notices of Proposed Adjustments (NOPAs) for those years. The report includes management's evaluation of disclosure controls and procedures, and the report of management on internal control over financial reporting. The auditor is Deloitte & Touche LLP, and the report is dated July 30, 2025.

children.summary: The report covers Microsoft Corporation's internal control over financial reporting as of June 30, 2025. Management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control, which provides reasonable assurance on the reliability of financial reporting. Management evaluated the effectiveness based on the COSO framework and concluded it was effective. No changes materially affected internal control during the quarter. Deloitte & Touche LLP audited the internal control and expressed an unqualified opinion, also auditing the consolidated financial statements with an unqualified opinion. The report includes the basis for opinion and definition of internal control.
